# SB-1010 Safety bulletin: noise exposure
Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01  

Hazard description
This bulletin addresses elevated noise exposure associated with Machining shot blast cabinet #1, identified as EQ-P3-L3-SB01. Prolonged or repeated exposure to high noise levels in the cabinet work area has the potential to produce permanent hearing loss and to impair communication critical for safe operation. Contributing factors observed during recent workplace reviews include reflected sound from the cabinet interior, tonal noise from drive and media delivery systems, and audible transients during loading and unloading of parts. Secondary hazards include reduced situational awareness leading to hand, arm, and general body injuries during maintenance and part handling, and increased likelihood of communication-related errors when coordinating work tasks.

Background and rationale
Cascade Forge Works conducted a targeted noise assessment in the vicinity of EQ-P3-L3-SB01 following operator reports and a comparison to historical maintenance records. The assessment identified consistent exceedances of recommended exposure actions in the operator workstation and immediate work envelope during normal processing cycles. Engineering controls were evaluated first by design review and cabinet acoustic path analysis. Administrative and personal protective equipment controls were also reviewed to provide layered protection pending completion of engineering improvements. This bulletin documents interim required controls and operational expectations to reduce risk and to standardize required records and follow-up actions.

Affected equipment
- Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) located on line P3-L3 at Plant P3.
- Adjacent operator workstation and immediate staging area used for loading and unloading parts for EQ-P3-L3-SB01.
- Any portable maintenance tools used inside the cabinet access zone during maintenance activities related to EQ-P3-L3-SB01.

Required controls
Engineering controls
- Operators and maintenance teams shall ensure that all cabinet access panels and acoustic seals are fully engaged prior to initiating the cabinet cycle. Damaged or missing seals identified during pre-use checks must be reported and replaced prior to operation.
- Use only approved maintenance consumables and lubricants for components associated with EQ-P3-L3-SB01. Lubricant part number: CFW-LUB-709 must be used for the Machining shot blast cabinet #1 lubrication points; document the application in the maintenance log when applied.
- Where practical, position sound-absorbing barrier material at known reflection points outside the cabinet to reduce operator exposure in the immediate work zone during load and unload tasks. Materials and placement shall be coordinated with maintenance engineering to avoid interference with ingress/egress and material handling.

Administrative controls
- Implement a pre-shift equipment check specific to EQ-P3-L3-SB01 that includes verification of acoustic seals, guard engagement, and confirmation of lubricant application when scheduled tasks require it. Findings from these checks must be entered into the equipment pre-use checklist and the shift log.
- Schedule noise mitigation maintenance work during lower-occupancy periods and coordinate with supervision to ensure fewer personnel are exposed during intrusive tasks.
- Limit the number of personnel in the immediate cabinet work envelope to those required to safely perform the task. When more than the required personnel are present, assign a lead communicator to coordinate tasks and ensure protective measures are followed.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
- When engineering and administrative controls do not reduce noise exposure to acceptable levels for the duration of the task, hearing protection devices approved by the site PPE committee shall be worn. Selection of hearing protection must be compatible with other PPE and communication needs for the task.

Work practice controls
- Use communication signals and standardized verbal confirmations for load and unload sequences to reduce unnecessary vocal strain and confusion in high-noise events.
- Minimize the duration spent with head in the immediate cabinet opening during active cycles. Use tools and extenders to position and remove parts where feasible.
- During maintenance or inspection tasks that require the cabinet to be open and systems energized, establish an exclusion zone and use documented lockout/tagout procedures referenced in SOP-P3-L3-02.

Examples and scenario guidance
- Example: During an unscheduled inspection, an operator discovers a torn acoustic seal on an access panel. The operator shall stop use of EQ-P3-L3-SB01, tag out the equipment, notify maintenance, and document the issue in the equipment pre-use checklist. Maintenance shall replace the seal and apply lubricant per approved schedule using lubricant part number: CFW-LUB-709 before returning EQ-P3-L3-SB01 to service.
- Example: For a routine media replenishment requiring the cabinet to be opened, the crew lead shall post the exclusion zone, verify PPE for everyone in the area, carry out the task in coordination with the operator, and log the activity in the maintenance record.

Records to keep
- Maintain the equipment pre-use checklist for EQ-P3-L3-SB01 in the shift log with any deficiencies and corrective actions noted.
- Record all maintenance activities related to noise control, including seal replacements, barrier installations, and lubricant applications. The lubrication entry must state lubricant part number: CFW-LUB-709 when that product is applied.
- Document noise assessment follow-up actions and verification testing results. Include references to related procedural requirements and verification steps in records as necessary.

Related documents
- Refer to MM-P3-L3-SB01 for mechanical maintenance procedures for shot blast cabinets.
- Refer to SOP-P3-L3-02 for lockout/tagout and isolation procedures when performing maintenance on equipment in line P3-L3.
- Refer to SOP-P3-L3-05 for operator pre-start and shift handover procedures applicable to EQ-P3-L3-SB01.

Effective date
This bulletin is effective immediately upon release. All affected personnel shall comply with the required controls and ensure records are updated as described. Supervisors are responsible for dissemination of this bulletin to affected teams and for coordinating any engineering mitigation actions with maintenance and plant safety.
